A cold distant sun hangs small and white, throwing long hard shadows across the graveyard's shattered bones.
A glowing nebula spreads behind the wrecks, its slow light catching broken edges in faint violet and blue.
A debris-dimmed starfield stretches beyond the boneyard, stars half-buried behind clouds of dust and drifting ash.
The aftermath-cloud of the battle still hangs thick, a pale haze curling slowly through the dead and silent fleet.
A ringed planet sits far beyond the graveyard, its cold bands tilted, indifferent to the wreckage below.
A blood-red dying star bleeds its weak light across the hulls, turning the boneyard the color of old rust.
Black void stretches in every direction, broken only by sparse and distant stars hanging cold and unreachable.
A green nebula drifts behind the dead hulls, tinting their scorched metal with a pale and sickly glow.
A far moon floats beyond the wreckage, grey and pocked, its silence matching the silence of the broken ships.
A faint galaxy band arcs across the dark, its soft blur of ancient light touching nothing in the cold boneyard.
A pale blue nebula breathes slowly behind the graveyard, its cold glow settling like frost across the ruined hulls.
Two dead moons hang at the edge of the field, their grey faces scarred, their orbits empty and slow.
A distant gas giant glows faint amber behind the wrecks, its storms invisible from here, its light barely reaching.
The starfield behind the boneyard is thin and scattered, stars few and far apart, the dark between them absolute.
A slow dust cloud drifts through the graveyard, dimming the stars behind it, swallowing the wreckage piece by piece.
A collapsed star pulses faintly at the edge of vision, its dim flicker cold and rhythmic over the dead fleet.
A pale white dwarf sits alone in the dark beyond, small and spent, casting almost nothing across the silent hulls.
A torn nebula hangs ragged behind the wrecks, its gases shredded by old shockwaves into long cold streamers.
The battle-cloud spreads wide and slow, catching starlight in its edges, a ghost of the violence that made the graveyard.
A red giant bleeds across the horizon of the boneyard, enormous and dying, its heat too far to reach the hulls.
A thin ring of debris circles a dead planet below, the boneyard and the world sharing the same cold orbit.
Dense shadow fills the graveyard where no star reaches, the hulls invisible at their centers, dark pressed against dark.
